title: Security Hardening
outcome: Threat-model TaskFlow and apply layered controls for access control, input/output safety, headers, abuse, secrets, uploads, dependencies, and configuration.
artifact: Security baseline checklist plus concrete tests for the most important abuse cases.
labSteps: List sensitive assets and trust boundaries before selecting mitigations.
Run an IDOR/broken-access-control test by changing resource IDs as another user.
Review all external input boundaries and confirm validation plus parameterized/ORM-safe persistence.
Review rendering/output paths for XSS assumptions and add sensible content/security headers.
Check secret locations, source control, logs, client bundles, CI, and deployment settings.
Add abuse controls where justified and write security regression tests for discovered cases.
failureModes: Security checklist with no threat model
Rate limiter treated as authentication or authorization
mastery: Can explain defense in depth and residual risk
principles: Threat-model trust boundaries before applying random security checklists.
Validate and authorize every sensitive server operation even if the frontend already restricts the UI.
Keep secrets out of source control, client bundles, logs, and error responses.
Use layered defenses for common web risks such as injection, broken access control, unsafe uploads, and misconfiguration.
